comparator.name: Physics & Astronomy
comparator.sourceNotes: Utrecht requires 90 EC of compulsory study, including the 15 EC research project, plus 45 EC of major electives and 45 EC of profiling electives. This example includes Atmosphere and Ocean Dynamics as a major elective. The other major electives remain open within Utrecht’s rules.

components.name: Bachelor Research Project

components.name: Required major choice
components.note: Choose Fluid Mechanics and Transport Phenomena or Structure of Matter.

components.name: Advanced major electives
components.note: Choose four approved level-3 courses. Climate-related examples include Geophysical Fluid Dynamics and Turbulence in Fluids.

components.name: Profiling electives

alternatives.concept: Use mathematics, programming and Earth observation to study how climate, oceans and land interact. Analyze Earth-system models and climate evidence, then apply that understanding to water management and renewable energy. Utrecht’s physics degree goes further into mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and astronomy.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One related-fields option is supported through Earth-system models, climate evidence and geospatial analysis, backed by sustained quantitative methods. Energy systems and coastal water management are applied extensions of the climate theme. Foundational sustainability courses provide some wave, optics, mechanics and thermodynamics study, while data and laboratory work support empirical inquiry. Neither strand supplies the cumulative physics foundation, instrumentation, or advanced study required for a separate physics or astronomy option.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop calculus for quantitative science.
Both develop linear algebra. Utrecht applies it within a physics sequence.
Both extend mathematical problem solving. UCR emphasizes numerical methods for equations and models.
Both develop empirical data analysis. Utrecht also teaches physics measurement and data acquisition.
Both study links between atmosphere, ocean and climate. UCR uses Earth-system models and tracers. Utrecht emphasizes the forces and equations governing circulation.
Utrecht develops classical and relativistic mechanics through a dedicated course.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course in electromagnetism.
Utrecht studies astronomy and optics. UCR introduces waves and spectroscopy in its sustainability gateway.
Utrecht provides a dedicated quantum mechanics course.
Utrecht develops statistical physics and experiments. UCR’s probability course supplies general statistical tools.

Utrecht requires a supervised physics project. Students normally complete the required taught courses and earn at least 90 EC before starting. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Utrecht requires an experimental physics project. UCR includes environmental fieldwork and data analysis.
Utrecht requires a choice between fluid mechanics and structure of matter.
Choose four level-3 courses. Utrecht offers geophysical fluid dynamics, turbulence and other advanced physics topics.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling electives.

notes.text: UCR offers a related plan in Earth systems and climate with mathematical modeling, remote sensing, water management and renewable energy. Utrecht provides dedicated study in mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics, astronomy and experimental physics, and requires a supervised physics research project.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Physics & Astronomy bachelor studies matter, forces, space and the climate system. Teaching starts in Dutch and uses more English in later years.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The comparison shows Utrecht’s required physics courses and elective rules, with Atmosphere and Ocean Dynamics as an example. UCR’s plan focuses on the Earth system, using mathematics, programming and observations to study climate and its effects.
